trace.step: Provider execution asks for allocator-backed builder

trace.step: Allocation alloc/grow failure normalization and ownership
facts: BufferAllocator is a marker over allocator_api2::Allocator + Debug + Send + Sync + static; BufferAllocatorRef::new wraps a shared custom allocator.
Allocator callbacks allocate, allocate_zeroed, grow, grow_zeroed, shrink return Result<NonNull<[u8]>, AllocError>; deallocate is callback.
Allocation retains the BufferAllocatorRef through owned buffer lifetime and Drop calls allocator.deallocate.

Allocation::allocate_impl unwraps allocation failure with handle_alloc_error(layout) at lines 274-295; Allocation::grow similarly unwraps allocate/grow failure with handle_alloc_error(new_layout) at lines 321-332. Neither path returns a VortexResult/Result from BufferMut constructors/growth.
BufferAllocatorRef implements Allocator with unsafe impl and forwards allocation/grow callbacks (lines 100-155).

The only public try_* methods in the fetched BufferMut file are try_extend_trusted and try_from_trusted_len_iter; their Result E is from iterator items (iter.process_results), while buffer allocation occurs through infallible constructors.
Buffer::try_into_mut returns Err(Self) when backing is non-Owned or Arc ownership cannot be extracted; it is an ownership uniqueness conversion, not an allocation-error Result.

blockers: Provider allocation/growth converts AllocError to handle_alloc_error rather than a typed recoverable VortexResult.
Custom BufferAllocator requires allocator_api2 unsafe Allocator implementation; current workspace forbids local unsafe code.
owner_hook_scope: Existing Bytes ownership wraps already-created buffers; it does not intercept provider builder allocation or growth.
